content: Magnesium hydroxide is a medication that is prescribed for short-term use to relieve constipation. In some cases, it may be recommended for other purposes, so it is important to consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information regarding its use. Magnesium hydroxide is available in both tablet and liquid forms, and it is taken orally. Typically, it is used as needed to address constipation. You should carefully follow the instructions provided on the packaging or your prescription label. If you have any questions or need clarification, ask your doctor or pharmacist. It is essential to take magnesium hydroxide exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of the medication, and do not use it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before starting magnesium hydroxide, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to this medication or other drugs. Additionally, provide them with a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins and supplements, that you are currently taking. Notify your doctor if you have a history of kidney disease or if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking magnesium hydroxide, contact your doctor immediately. If you are taking magnesium hydroxide as needed, there is no specific dosing schedule. However, if your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly and you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Magnesium hydroxide may cause side effects. If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: stomach cramps, upset stomach, vomiting, or diarrhea. If you encounter a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program either online or by phone. Store magnesium hydroxide in its original container, ensuring that it is tightly closed and kept out of reach of children. Store it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on safe disposal. If you have any additional questions about magnesium hydroxide, do not hesitate to ask your pharmacist. This medication is available under brand names such as Milk of Magnesia®, Milk of Magnesia-Concentrated®, and Phillips Milk of Magnesia®.
